messages.author: 660737e3448b7bb7
messages.subject: How to vectorize pow()
parts:
The lines

for (i in 1:N) {
thesd[i] <- pow(pow(sds[i],2)*booterror+pow(lowsd,2),0.5);
}

are really slowing down my code, and I'm wondering if there is anyway to vectorize the power function, or some other way around this. The standard deviation for each of my observations is based on a measurement error previously calculated for each observation (sds) and a model error (lowsd). My full code is pretty long and confusing, but the following simpler model basically shows what I am doing although it is overparameterized in a way that my real model isn't.

 testcode <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector[N] y;
  real sds[N];
} 

parameters {
real mu;
real<lower=0,upper=100> lowsd;
real<lower=0,upper=100> booterror;
corr_matrix[N] meascorr;
} 

transformed parameters {
vector[N] muvec;
vector[N] thesd;
for (i in 1:N) {
thesd[i] <- pow(pow(sds[i],2)*booterror+pow(lowsd,2),0.5);
muvec[i] <- mu;
}
}

model {
meascorr ~ lkj_corr(2);
mu ~ normal(0, 10);
y ~ multi_normal(muvec, diag_matrix(thesd)*meascorr*diag_matrix(thesd)); 
}
"

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: How to vectorize pow()
parts:
On Tuesday, May 7, 2013 1:16:37 PM UTC-4, Spencer Maynes wrote:
The lines

for (i in 1:N) {
thesd[i] <- pow(pow(sds[i],2)*booterror+pow(lowsd,2),0.5);
}

are really slowing down my code, and I'm wondering if there is anyway to vectorize the power function, or some other way around this.

There isn't a version of the pow() function that accepts a vector, so what you have there is basically the way to do it. It might be slightly faster if you would use the square() and sqrt() functions instead of the the pow(x,k) function that takes an arbitrary exponent. But I doubt that is slowing you down a noticeable amount. If there were a Stan version of the pow() function that accepted a vector, it would compile to essentially the same thing that the above loop compiles to. If you profiled

http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Profiling-compiled-code

the model, I'm almost positive that the C++ translation of these function calls

meascorr ~ lkj_corr(2);
y ~ multi_normal(muvec, diag_matrix(thesd)*meascorr*diag_matrix(thesd));

would be taking up most of the computation time.

Ben

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: How to vectorize pow()
parts:
As Ben said, it's unlikely that the pow() calls are the slow parts of
this model. Why do you think it's that line that is slowing things
down?

I assume that N is fairly large, in which case you might be able to
speed up this line:

y ~ multi_normal(muvec, diag_matrix(thesd)*meascorr*diag_matrix(thesd));

by dividing y and muvec by thesd.

(y./thesd) ~ mult_normal(muvec./thesd,meascorr);

If thesd was a parameter, you'd also need to do a correction to lp__:

lp__ <- lp__ - sum(log(thesd))

but since thesd is data, this would just be a constant and is unnecessary.

Hope this helps a bit.

Cheers,
Marcus
